title: Boundary characterization of a relative initial or final object
statement: Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $\partial\Delta^n$ for the simplicial union of the proper faces of $\Delta^n$. Let $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, meaning that it lifts every inner horn. Call $x\in\mathcal X$ $p$-initial if $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(p(x),p(z))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $z\in\mathcal X$. This holds if and only if, for every $n>0$, every square $\partial\Delta^n\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal X$, $\Delta^n\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ with $pa=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ and $a(0)=x$ has a filler $\widetilde b$ satisfying both equations $p\widetilde b=b$ and $\widetilde b|_{\partial\Delta^n}=a$. Dually define $p$-final by the weak equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(z,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(p(z),p(x))$ for all $z$; it is equivalent to the boundary-filling condition with $a(n)=x$. There is no dimension-zero filling requirement.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, conditions (1) and (3), with the relative-initial mapping-space meaning of Proposition 7.1.5.16 (02WR), and their opposite duals. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online source, archive wanted.

proof.text:
Fix the specified vertex $x$ and first prove the final-vertex assertion. Use the join slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] to set $E=\mathcal X_{/x}$ and $T=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y_{/p(x)}$. Define $q:E\to T$ by $\sigma\mapsto(\sigma|_{\Delta^m},p\sigma)$ in degree $m$, viewing $\sigma$ as a map $\Delta^{m+1}=\Delta^m\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal X$ whose last vertex is $x$. The pullback equation is precisely restriction of $p\sigma$ to the initial face spanned by $0,\ldots,m$. For each vertex $z\in\mathcal X$, take the degreewise fibers over the projection $T\to\mathcal X$. The slice statement identifies the resulting map exactly with
$$q_z:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(z,x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(p(z),p(x)).$$
Both these mapping simplicial sets are Kan complexes. These are the right-pinched spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so no change of mapping-space model is being made.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17 and the opposite dual, expanded slice construction; Proposition 7.1.5.16(2); Proposition 4.3.6.1 (018F) and Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX).

proof.text:
The map $q$ is a right fibration in the horn-lifting sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Indeed, a lifting problem for $\Lambda_i^m\subseteq\Delta^m$, with $m\geq1$ and $0<i\leq m$, unpacks by the slice formula of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] into a lifting problem for $p$ on
$$D=(\Lambda_i^m\star\Delta^0)\cup_{\Lambda_i^m}\Delta^m\subseteq\Delta^m\star\Delta^0=\Delta^{m+1}.$$
Here $\Delta^m$ is the face opposite the last vertex and the new last vertex has prescribed value $x$. The faces of $D$ are the face $\Delta^m$ opposite the last vertex and the cones on the faces of $\Delta^m$ other than its $i$th face. Thus $D=\Lambda_i^{m+1}$. The inequality $0<i<m+1$ makes this horn inner, so the assumed inner fibration $p$ gives the required filler. Its restriction to the last vertex remains $x$, hence it is exactly a filler for the original square of $q$. This also covers $m=1,i=1$.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.6.9 (01C0), right-slice case with K the point; explicit inner-horn calculation underlying Corollary 7.1.5.17.

proof.text: The map $q_z$ in step 1 is the pullback of $q$ along the inclusion $\{z\}\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y_{/p(x)}\to T$. Right-horn lifting is preserved under this pullback: solve a projected lifting problem for $q$ and pair its filler with the prescribed map into the pullback base; the pullback equation holds because the filler projects to that prescribed map. Therefore $q_z$ is a right fibration. Its base $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(p(z),p(x))$ is Kan by step 1. Apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] to conclude that $q_z$ lifts every horn, so it is a Kan fibration. We use only the Kan-fibration clause of that node, not its additional homotopy-fiber assertion.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5.16(2), fiberwise comparison expanded using Corollary 4.4.3.8 (01NV).

proof.text:
Suppose $x$ is $p$-final. Then every $q_z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by the definition in the item. Since it is a Kan fibration, [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] says that each of its vertex fibers is a contractible Kan complex. Every vertex of $T$ is a pair $(z,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(z)\to p(x)$, and the fiber of $q$ at this pair is degreewise exactly the fiber of $q_z$ at $\alpha$. Thus all vertex fibers of the right fibration $q$ are contractible. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] to obtain that $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration.
Conversely, suppose $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Every boundary lifting problem for its pullback $q_z$ projects to one for $q$; pair the resulting filler with the prescribed map into the pullback base. This proves boundary lifting for $q_z$ in every dimension, including dimension zero. By step 3 it is a Kan fibration, so [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] makes it a weak homotopy equivalence. This holds for every $z$, which is precisely $p$-finality. Hence $x$ is $p$-final if and only if $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, equivalence (1) and (2), opposite dual; replacement of the categorical-equivalence intermediate by the explicit fiber argument of Propositions 3.3.7.6 (00ZP) and 4.4.2.14 (01NU).

proof.text:
Unpack boundary lifting for $q$ using [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] and the slice formula of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. A square $\partial\Delta^m\to E$ over $\Delta^m\to T$ consists of a prescribed map $c:\Delta^m\to\mathcal X$, a map $d:\Delta^{m+1}\to\mathcal Y$ with $d(m+1)=p(x)$ and $d|_{\Delta^m}=pc$, and a compatible map $(\partial\Delta^m)\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal X$ with last vertex $x$ over the corresponding restriction of $d$. The last vertex is fixed at $x$ by the definition of the slices. When $m=0$, the upper map $\partial\Delta^0\to E$ is empty, but the cone on its empty domain is the single fixed vertex $x$. Glue the two maps into $\mathcal X$ on
$$(\partial\Delta^m\star\Delta^0)\cup_{\partial\Delta^m}\Delta^m=\partial\Delta^{m+1}.$$
This equality follows face by face: the face opposite the last vertex is $\Delta^m$ and all other faces are cones on its proper faces. A filler for the square of $q$ is consequently exactly a filler of this boundary over $d$, with both required simplicial equalities. Conversely, any positive-dimensional boundary square for $p$ whose last vertex is $x$ decomposes into these data by restricting to the face opposite the last vertex and to the union of all remaining faces. Thus the correspondence works in both directions. At $m=0$ it identifies surjectivity of $q_0$ with the $n=1$ boundary lifting condition for $p$, fixing the two endpoints. As $n=m+1$, all $m\geq0$ for $q$ are exactly all $n>0$ for $p$. Combining this with step 4 proves the final-vertex assertion, without any dimension-zero condition for $p$.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, equivalence (2) and (3), opposite dual; degreewise join/slice adjunction with the dimension-zero slice case included.

proof.text:
Pass to opposites to obtain the initial-vertex assertion. Explicitly, for a simplicial set $C$ define $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ by replacing an operator $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ with $j\mapsto b-\alpha(a-j)$. Reversal is involutive, carries $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, and preserves whole boundaries. Thus $\mathcal X^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ are quasicategories and $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an inner fibration; a boundary with first vertex $x$ becomes one with last vertex $x$, preserving its restriction and projection equations.
For the mapping-space condition use [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. With its Kan arrow mapping spaces $U$, reversal gives a simplicial isomorphism
$$U_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b)\cong U_C(b,a)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
To check this isomorphism in degree $m$, represent a simplex of $U_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b)$ by its prism $f:\Delta^1\times\Delta^m\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply the opposite operation to $f$ and precompose with the vertex-reversal identifications $\Delta^1\cong(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\Delta^m\cong(\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The resulting prism into $C$ has endpoints $b,a$. For $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$, restriction of this prism uses the reversed operator $j\mapsto m-\alpha(r-j)$; these are exactly the operators of $U_C(b,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing twice returns $f$, and applying a simplicial functor commutes with every operation, proving both the isomorphism and its naturality. For any simplicial set $Z$, barycentric reversal $(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\mapsto(t_n,\ldots,t_0)$ defines a natural homeomorphism $|Z^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|Z|$: the relation for $\alpha$ on one side is the relation for its reversed operator on the other. Combine these homeomorphisms with the natural right-pinch homotopy equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b)\longrightarrow U_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b),\qquad
\operatorname{Map}_C(b,a)\longrightarrow U_C(b,a).$$
Naturality under $p$ identifies, up to these equivalences on source and target, the incoming mapping-space maps of $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ at $x$ with the outgoing mapping-space maps of $p$ at $x$. By the weak homotopy equivalence convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], one family consists of weak homotopy equivalences if and only if the other does (check components and each based homotopy group through this commuting comparison). Therefore $p$-initiality is equivalent to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-finality. Apply steps 1-5 to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse the resulting fillers. This proves both implications of the initial-vertex assertion with exactly the original hypotheses.
